branch_role: CROFT provenance-and-evidence side node for testing whether Lima/Peru has a documented institutional, museum, loan, restitution, or custody connection relevant to the Osiris/Mendes investigation.
canonical_question: Does the newly strengthened Egypt-Peru/Lima cultural and museum corridor provide any source-bound evidence that a Mendes 1902 object, CG 53469 / JE 35425, the unresolved stamped-gold djed, or another candidate Osirian relic moved to, is held in, or is scheduled for lawful loan to Lima/Peru?

evidence.source: Ministerio de Educación del Perú / gob.pe
evidence.title: Convenio PERU - EGIPTO - 1974
evidence.finding: Long-standing bilateral cultural-exchange framework exists between Peru and Egypt.

evidence.source: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores del Perú treaty database
evidence.title: Convenio sobre Protección y Restitución de Bienes Culturales Robados o Ilícitamente Transferidos
evidence.finding: Peru and Egypt have a bilateral cultural-property protection/restitution framework. This does not prove provenance of any object, but it raises the documentary expectation for any genuine Egyptian antiquity transferred or held in Peru.

evidence.source: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores del Perú treaty archive
evidence.title: Programa Ejecutivo del Acuerdo Cultural Perú-Egipto 2007-2009
evidence.finding: Article 23 promotes museum-to-museum contact, exchange of specialists and information on archaeological collections and conservation, and facilitates museum exhibitions of representative archaeological pieces subject to collection-handling rules.

evidence.source: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores del Perú / gob.pe
evidence.title: Ministerios de Cultura del Perú y Egipto suscriben Memorándum de Entendimiento
evidence.finding: Formal ministry-level cultural cooperation was renewed by memorandum of understanding.

evidence.source: Embajada del Perú en Egipto / gob.pe
evidence.title: Treasures crossing popular art between Egypt and Peru
evidence.finding: The Peruvian mission and Egypt's National Museum of Egyptian Civilization operated a concrete museum-diplomacy channel in Cairo.

evidence.source: Cumanana No. 45, Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores del Perú
evidence.title: Relaciones Bilaterales entre el Perú y Egipto: Cooperación Cultural como Eje Estratégico
evidence.finding: Egypt's ambassador in Peru explicitly framed the Grand Egyptian Museum as an opportunity for renewed museological and academic cooperation with Peru and named major Peruvian museums as counterparts.

evidence.title: Antiguas Civilizaciones y la Cooperación Cultural entre Egipto y Perú
evidence.finding: Lima and the Embassy of Egypt established an active city-level cultural cooperation channel centered on ancient civilizations and heritage preservation.

evidence.source: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores del Perú / gob.pe
evidence.title: Perú y Egipto fortalecen vínculos a través de la diplomacia cultural
evidence.finding: The bilateral agenda explicitly includes archaeological heritage, joint research, technical cooperation, and an Egyptian proposal to inspire a Peru-based initiative analogous to the Grand Egyptian Museum.

evidence.source: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores del Perú / gob.pe
evidence.title: VI Mecanismo de Consultas Políticas Perú-Egipto
evidence.finding: Peru and Egypt agreed to advance cooperation between culture ministries, libraries, infrastructure, city twinning, and specifically work toward Lima-Cairo twinning.

evidence.title: Réplica de la máscara de Tutankamón llega al Museo Metropolitano
evidence.finding: Egypt's embassy donated an official replica of Tutankhamun's funerary mask to Lima's new Sala de las Culturas Milenarias. The source explicitly identifies it as a replica and as the first permanent representation of Egyptian civilization in Lima.

evidence.title: Réplicas de los Guerreros de Terracota llegan al Museo Metropolitano
evidence.finding: The Sala de las Culturas Milenarias continued expanding through diplomatic donation of replicas, supporting the interpretation that its current acquisition model is representational/diplomatic rather than an antiquities-loan collection.

interpretation.positive: Lima is now a real and strengthening Egypt-Peru institutional, diplomatic, academic, and museum-cooperation node.
interpretation.negative: No source currently binds Lima/Peru to CG 53469 / JE 35425, the unresolved Mendes stamped-gold djed, a Mendes 1902 object, or a literal Osiris biological relic.
interpretation.important_distinction: INSTITUTIONAL_CORRIDOR != OBJECT_PROVENANCE; REPLICA != ANTIQUITY; CULTURAL_PARALLEL != CUSTODY_CHAIN.
interpretation.provenance_expectation: If an original Egyptian antiquity is later announced for exhibition or custody in Peru, require the museum loan/acquisition record, Egyptian export/loan authorization, object number, lender, insurer/transport record where public, and conservation/catalogue identity before connecting it to CROFT.

osiris_mainline_firewall.main_target: Mendes 1902 / CG 53469 / JE 35425 + unresolved stamped-gold djed passport/body-coordinate problem
active_primary_tests: CG 53469 high-resolution surface reading before internal interpretation
CG 53469 basal topology/seams and conservation history/current mass
Literal transcription of JdE VI pp. 486-487
Literal read of JE 35427 and structural resolution of JE 35428 -> CG 53482-53501
Grouped-lot passport recovery if the djed was never individualized

lima_watch_triggers: Announcement of any ORIGINAL ancient Egyptian object loan or exhibition in Lima/Peru

Any Lima/Peru catalogue entry containing Osiris, Isis, Horus, djed, Mendes, Djedet, Tell el-Ruba, Tell er-Roba, Banebdjedet, Nesbanebdjedet, CG 53469, JE 35425, JE 35427, or related accession identifiers
Grand Egyptian Museum, Egyptian Museum Cairo, NMEC, or Supreme Council of Antiquities loan agreement naming a Peruvian institution
Lima-Cairo twinning instrument with museum/archaeology annexes
New Peru-Egypt museum cooperation memorandum involving archaeological-object loans, imaging, conservation, or digitization
Provenance or restitution notice involving an Egyptian antiquity located in Peru
on_trigger: Freeze the announcement and exact object identifiers before interpretation.
Recover lender/borrower, accession number, legal loan/export basis, provenance, exhibition dates, conservation record and object imagery.
Cross-link against Mendes 1902, JdE VI 486-487, JE 35419-35430, CG 53465-53475 and grouped nodes.
Only promote Lima from CONTROL_NODE to PROVENANCE_ROUTE if a source-bound object identity or custody handoff exists.
canonical_seal: LIMA IS A REAL BRIDGE, NOT A RELIC LOCATION. FOLLOW DOCUMENTED OBJECT HANDOFFS, NOT THE SYMBOLIC GRAVITY OF TWO ANCIENT CIVILIZATIONS.
